title: Merlin and Atlan's unfinished train, souvenirs and work schedule
summary: She describes the long build, doubts it will be finished, and how many nights they work on it; the interviewer asks about labels to take back. They play jazz only in winter and spring.

And on the table, on the table, they have installed a whole and the American locomotive, the old, of the last century. And they tried to reconstitue the New Orléans in the last century. The ceiling represents the sky, it is blue with some clouds. On the walls, there is a campagin, all over with the trees. And there is the Mississippi, of course. There was a problem with the Mississippi, because it had to be as warm as possible. They tried to have the water tinted, color, with a sort of colorant brun. But it didn't happen because the colorant was placed in the bottom and the water remained clean. They put a kind of plastic plastic brun which imite very well the water. They are very happy like that. I suggested to put the real water, but they thought that it would not be. And then there are all the rues of the New Orléans. There is the gare, the waterfront, the French street, with the small houses, with the balcony of the fer forgers. There are the dogs, I already said, the Canal Street, and the campagnes, they also have made parks. But they stopped there because at the moment they haven't finished. They work a lot, they spend all their hours. So every morning, we see them with a marteau, a turn-in, working on the side, but it's never finished, and it never works. I haven't seen the train work. I haven't seen the train work. The decor is almost finished, but it's not that. I think it will never work. I think it will never work.
It's finished. It's finished. The trains never run. It's not that.
Yeah. But I wondered, are you going to take them any souvenirs back which they could use and to add on, you know, like advertising from packages, or anything printed they could put on the trucks?

Well, we'll look as we go around. We'll look for things. You know, labels, I'm talking about. You know what I mean, perhaps. Do they use those already? Yes. They have those already. Do you remember any of the companies that they've saved? Do the names mean anything to you?
Yes, but they're typical New Orleans things, if they say, that's it. Did you say that you think they will finish it someday or not?
I don't think so. That's too much work, I think. I hope so.
How many nights a week do they work on it?
Oh, almost three and four. And the weekend, Saturday and Sunday too, when they are not playing jazz.
Yes. Or once a month. And more when .
When you hear them play? Yes. And they, but they don't play during the summer.
No. They play just in winter and spring, and they stop in May to October.
